objective: P1 of the planner-web pivot: turn the P0 shell into a working interview. A researcher pastes a paragraph describing their experiment, the app deterministically extracts what it can, asks the smallest set of questions needed to fill the rest, expands the design into concrete condition rows with sample IDs, and renders the resulting filenames -- all with the LLM switched off.
demoable_outcome: paragraph -> questions -> sample IDs -> filenames, entirely deterministic.

decisions.kb_delivery: web/kb/*.json, embedded at build into globalThis.__MICRONAUT_KB__ by the existing tools/build_single_file.py _load_kb; the loader is a PURE function taking the raw object so it is testable under node --test with no globals.
decisions.kb_generation: web/kb/markers.json is GENERATED from src/microscopy_naming_assistant/markers.py by tools/export_markers_kb.py and gated by a pytest that regenerates and diffs. Per lesson 40 the JS-side marker table must never be a hand-retyped copy of the Python producer.
decisions.predicate_dsl: small JSON boolean language evaluated against the Experiment via core/paths.js getPath. No eval(), no Function(). TOTAL: a missing path or unknown operator yields false, never a throw -- a malformed KB rule must not white-screen the app.
decisions.provenance: everything the interview or the free-text parser writes is WEAK or PROVISIONAL, never STRONG. Only a direct user answer is 'user'. This is enforced by C0-2's canOverwrite, so a re-parse can never clobber a typed answer.
decisions.llm: still absent in P1. Every P1 feature must work with the LLM off; the LLM seam is P3.

invariants: web/ never imports from src/ - the two products share generated data files only
No fetch() in the released artifact
No type=module, dynamic import, or top-level await in the released artifact
Every top-level declared symbol name is unique across web/src/** (exported OR private - the build gate now checks both)
Every feature fully usable with the LLM disabled

Python gate: pytest -q -m 'not integration' stays green (Classic must not regress)
JS gate: node --test web/tests/*.test.js (NOT 'node --test web/tests/', which fails MODULE_NOT_FOUND on node v22), no node_modules ever created

tasks.title: Knowledge pack: generated marker KB + pure loader/validate/index
tasks.scope:
Stand up the knowledge pack and the code that loads it.

(1) tools/export_markers_kb.py (Python 3.10+, STDLIB ONLY apart from importing the project's own markers module): import src/microscopy_naming_assistant/markers.py and emit web/kb/markers.json. READ markers.py FIRST -- do not retype its contents. The emitted JSON must be deterministic (sort_keys, stable separators, trailing newline) so two runs are byte-identical. Shape:
  {
    "version": 1,
    "markers": { "<CANONICAL>": { "aliases": [...lowercased, sorted...], "freeTextAliases": [...aliases MINUS anything in AMBIGUOUS_IN_FREE_TEXT...], "class": "dye|protein|tag|moiety|stain|indicator", "isFamily": bool, "variants": [...] } },
    "ambiguousInFreeText": [...sorted...]
  }
The `class`/`isFamily`/`variants` fields resolve the content prerequisite the parent plan flagged: MITOTRACKER, LYSOTRACKER, SYTOX, GCAMP and BODIPY are FAMILIES spanning several spectra (isFamily true, variants listing the spelled-out members already present in their alias lists, e.g. mitotracker red/green/deep red/orange); HALO, SNAP and CLIP are protein TAGS with no spectrum of their own (class 'tag'); PHALLOIDIN and WGA are targeting MOIETIES with no spectrum (class 'moiety'). Everything else defaults to class 'dye' unless it is plainly a fluorescent protein (GFP/RFP/CFP/YFP/BFP/MCHERRY/TDTOMATO/MNEONGREEN/MSCARLET/MTURQUOISE/CERULEAN/VENUS/CITRINE/IRFP/MIRFP/MEMERALD/MRUBY -> 'protein') or a calcium indicator (FLUO4/FURA2/GCAMP -> 'indicator'). Derive these classifications in the exporter as explicit literal sets so they are reviewable in one place; do NOT guess per-marker at runtime.

(2) tests/test_markers_kb_export.py (pytest): regenerate the KB into tmp_path and assert byte-equality with the committed web/kb/markers.json, so a markers.py edit that is not re-exported FAILS the Python gate instead of silently shipping a stale table. Also assert the exporter is deterministic across two runs, that every ambiguousInFreeText entry is absent from every marker's freeTextAliases, and that freeTextAliases is a subset of aliases.

(3) web/src/core/kb.js: PURE functions, no globals read at module scope. Export loadKb(raw) -> {kb, issues} which validates the raw object (missing/!=version -> a fatal issue; a marker entry missing `aliases` -> an issue naming the marker) and returns an indexed structure, indexKb(kb) building { aliasToCanonical: Map, freeTextAliasToCanonical: Map, canonicals: [...] } with LOWERCASED keys, and kbMarker(kb, canonical). Validation must be TOTAL: never throw on a malformed KB, always return issues, because a bad KB must degrade to 'no markers known', not a white screen.

(4) Wire delivery in both modes. tools/build_single_file.py already embeds web/kb/*.json into globalThis.__MICRONAUT_KB__ at build (see _load_kb) -- confirm that path works with a real web/kb/ present now that the directory exists. For the DEV (unbuilt) page, make the build also emit web/kb.dev.js (a single line assigning the same global) and point web/index.html's BUILD:KB dev block at it with a classic <script src="./kb.dev.js"></script> (classic script src works over both http:// and file://; fetch() does not, and is forbidden anyway). Add web/kb.dev.js to .gitignore -- it is a generated artifact.

INVARIANTS FOR THIS TASK: no fetch(); no top-level await; kb.js must not read globalThis at module scope (that is main.js's job in C1-6); every new top-level symbol name must be unique across web/src/** or the build's duplicate-declaration gate will hard-fail.
tasks.verification: `python tools/export_markers_kb.py` writes web/kb/markers.json and running it twice produces byte-identical output. `python -m pytest -q tests/test_markers_kb_export.py` passes, and PROVE the staleness gate is live rather than vacuous: temporarily add a marker to markers.py, re-run the test, confirm it FAILS, revert, confirm it passes again. `node --test web/tests/*.test.js` passes with the new kb.test.js, which must prove: a KB with the wrong version returns a fatal issue and does NOT throw; a marker missing `aliases` is reported by name; indexKb maps a known alias ('af488') to its canonical ('ALEXA488') case-insensitively; every entry of ambiguousInFreeText is absent from freeTextAliasToCanonical while still present in aliasToCanonical (this is the whole point of the two maps). `python tools/build_single_file.py --out dist/` still succeeds and dist/index.html now contains __MICRONAUT_KB__ with real marker data. Confirm no node_modules exists and `pytest -q -m 'not integration'` is still green.

tasks.title: Predicate DSL: total, eval-free rule evaluation against the Experiment
tasks.scope:
web/src/engine/predicate.js -- the small boolean language that decides when a question gets asked (C1-3) and, later, when a control rule applies (P2). It is the reason the question bank and control rules can be DATA rather than code.

Export evaluatePredicate(pred, experiment) -> boolean and describePredicate(pred) -> string (a short human-readable rendering, used by the UI to explain WHY a question is being asked -- the parent plan's 'the why, not just the what' principle).

Grammar (JSON, no eval(), no new Function() -- the released artifact is a single inlined script and must stay auditable):
  leaf:   {"eq": ["<path>", value]} | {"ne": [...]} | {"in": ["<path>", [v1, v2]]} | {"gt": ["<path>", n]} | {"lt": ["<path>", n]} | {"exists": "<path>"} | {"empty": "<path>"} | {"matches": ["<path>", "<regex source>"]}
  branch: {"all": [...]} | {"any": [...]} | {"not": pred}
  literal: true | false
Paths are resolved with core/paths.js getPath, so 'panel.channels[0].marker' works. `exists` is true when the value is not undefined/null AND not an empty string/array. `matches` MUST anchor the whole string using engine/validation.js compileFullMatch -- do NOT hand-roll a RegExp, or the Python/JS anchoring landmine C0-4 fixed comes straight back in a second place.

TOTALITY IS THE CENTRAL REQUIREMENT: this evaluates author-written data, so it must NEVER throw. A missing path, an unknown operator, a malformed node (wrong arity, non-array where an array is required), a null predicate, or a bad regex source all evaluate to FALSE. An undefined predicate (no condition given) evaluates to TRUE -- a question with no askWhen is always askable. A cyclic/deeply-nested predicate must not blow the stack: cap recursion depth at 32 and return false beyond it.

INVARIANTS: imports only from core/paths.js and engine/validation.js; no DOM; no globals; no top-level await; unique top-level symbol names across web/src/**.
tasks.verification: `node --test web/tests/*.test.js` passes. The tests must PROVE totality by execution, not by inspection -- assert.doesNotThrow (or equivalent) plus a false result for each of: unknown operator, missing path, null/undefined predicate node, wrong-arity leaf, non-array argument to all/any, and an invalid regex source. Prove `undefined` predicate -> true while `null` -> false. Prove the anchoring: a predicate {"matches": ["naming.fields.sample", "[A-Za-z0-9_-]+"]} against the value 'bad note' must be FALSE (a naive unanchored RegExp.test would say true) -- this is the C0-4 landmine re-proven in its new home. Prove nesting depth is capped by feeding a 40-deep {"not": {"not": ...}} chain and getting false rather than a RangeError. Prove describePredicate returns a non-empty string for every operator in the grammar.

tasks.title: Condition matrix: factors x levels x replicates -> condition rows -> sample IDs
tasks.scope:
web/src/engine/conditions.js -- expand a design into the concrete rows that become sample IDs and therefore filenames. Pure module, no DOM, no store.

Export:
  expandConditions(design) -> [{ id, factorLevels: {factorName: level}, replicate }]  -- the full cartesian product of every factor's levels, repeated for each replicate (1..design.replicates). Deterministic ORDER is part of the contract: factors in their declared order, levels in their declared order, replicate varying fastest. Downstream naming depends on this, so the tests must pin the exact sequence.
  buildSampleId(row, scheme) -> string -- render a row through an id scheme template like '{genotype}{treatment}R{replicate}' using the same {token} syntax as the naming template, then sanitize it. REUSE engine/naming.js sanitizeToken for that sanitization rather than writing a second sanitizer; a divergence between sample IDs and filename tokens is exactly the kind of silent inconsistency this project keeps getting bitten by. An unknown token in the scheme is an ERROR surfaced as an issue, not a silent empty string.
  conditionIssues(design) -> [{field, message, severity}] using the SAME {field,message,severity} shape as engine/validation.js validationIssue, so the UI renders design problems and naming problems through one code path.

Guardrails the tests must pin: zero factors is legal (a single unconditioned sample); a factor with zero levels yields ZERO rows and an issue (not a silent empty product); replicates defaults to 1 when null/absent and an issue is raised for replicates < 1; duplicate factor names raise an issue; the combinatorial size is capped (refuse to expand beyond 1000 rows, returning an issue) so a fat-fingered design cannot hang the browser building millions of rows.

INVARIANTS: imports only from engine/naming.js (for sanitizeToken); no DOM; no top-level await; unique top-level symbol names across web/src/**.
tasks.verification: `node --test web/tests/*.test.js` passes. Prove by executed assertion, not inspection: the EXACT row sequence for 2 factors (2 levels x 3 levels) with 2 replicates -- 12 rows in the documented order, asserted as a full deepEqual against a literal expected array, so any future reordering fails loudly. Prove zero factors -> exactly one row. Prove a factor with zero levels -> zero rows AND an issue. Prove replicates=null defaults to 1. Prove an unknown token in the id scheme surfaces an issue rather than rendering an empty segment. Prove the >1000-row cap returns an issue and does not attempt the expansion (time the call or assert the returned row count is 0). Prove buildSampleId's output for a level containing a space or slash matches what engine/naming.js sanitizeToken produces for the same input -- call sanitizeToken directly in the test to compare, rather than hardcoding the expected string.

tasks.title: Deterministic free-text ingest: paragraph -> provisional field proposals
tasks.scope:
web/src/engine/freetext.js -- the headline demo: a researcher pastes a paragraph and the app extracts what it can WITH THE LLM OFF. This is the deterministic tier that must always work; the LLM (P3) only ever upgrades comprehension on top of it.

READ src/microscopy_naming_assistant/metadata.py::_extract_markers FIRST and port its exact matching semantics -- do NOT re-derive them from memory or from this description. That function encodes hard-won behaviour: it scans with re.finditer (NOT re.search -- see the repo's B2/B3 defect history where one-match-per-alias silently dropped a real second fluorophore), matches on WORD BOUNDARIES, and resolves overlapping alias hits by LONGEST-MATCH-WINS so 'ATTO 647-N' yields ATTO647N rather than ATTO647 plus a stray N. Reproduce that overlap resolution exactly; it is the single most defect-prone part of this task.

Export parseFreeText(text, index) -> { proposals: [{path, value, tag, evidence, confidence}], unmatched: [...] } where `index` is C1-1's indexKb output. Use ONLY freeTextAliasToCanonical for prose scanning -- never aliasToCanonical -- because the AMBIGUOUS_IN_FREE_TEXT list exists precisely to stop 'snap', 'halo', 'clip', 'venus', 'citrine', 'emerald', 'cerulean' and 'tomato' from false-positiving in ordinary English. Ignoring that distinction is the defining failure mode of this task.

Also extract, with plain anchored regexes:
  - replicates: 'n=3', 'n = 3', '3 replicates', 'triplicate' (->3), 'duplicate' (->2)
  - magnification: '63x', '63X', 'x63' -> normalized like Classic's parser. READ src/microscopy_naming_assistant/metadata.py's magnification parser first; it was fixed once already to anchor on the unit rather than on a bare number, and re-deriving it will reintroduce that bug.
  - a date in ISO form (YYYY-MM-DD) only -- do NOT attempt to parse ambiguous formats like 03/04/2026, whose meaning differs by locale. Ambiguity here silently mislabels data.
Every proposal carries `evidence`: the exact substring matched, with its index, so the UI can show the user WHY a value was proposed.

PROVENANCE: every proposal is tagged 'freetext' (WEAK). This module NEVER writes to the store and never emits 'user'. C0-2's canOverwrite then structurally guarantees a re-parse cannot clobber an answer the user typed.

Create tests/fixtures/freetext_conformance.json -- shared paragraphs + expected canonical marker sets, read by BOTH web/tests/freetext.test.js AND a Python counterpart assertion path where the Python extractor is expected to agree, following the tests/fixtures/regex_conformance.json precedent from C0-4. Where JS and Python are INTENDED to differ, say so explicitly in the fixture entry rather than omitting the case.

INVARIANTS: imports only from core/kb.js (types) and engine/naming.js if needed; no DOM; no store writes; no top-level await; unique top-level symbol names across web/src/**.
tasks.verification: `node --test web/tests/*.test.js` passes. Prove the ported semantics against the ACTUAL Python producer, not against memory: for each fixture paragraph, run src/microscopy_naming_assistant/metadata.py's marker extraction over the same text and confirm the canonical SETS agree (compare as sets -- repo lesson E3 notes marker ORDER is not stable and is not what is under test). MUST prove, by executed assertion: 'ch1 ATTO 647-N ch2 ATTO 647' yields BOTH ATTO647N and ATTO647 (the finditer/longest-match behaviour -- a re.search-style port silently drops one, which is the exact defect this repo already shipped once); a paragraph containing the sentence 'we took a snap of the halo around the tomato explant' yields ZERO markers (the AMBIGUOUS_IN_FREE_TEXT exclusion doing its job) while the metadata value 'HaloTag' still resolves via the full alias map; 'n=3' / 'triplicate' / '3 replicates' all yield replicates 3; '63x' and 'x63' normalize identically; '03/04/2026' yields NO date proposal. Prove every emitted proposal carries tag 'freetext' and a non-empty evidence substring that is genuinely present in the input at the stated index. Confirm the module performs no store writes (grep it for setPath/store and confirm absent).

tasks.title: Interview engine: question bank, next-question selection, answer recording
tasks.scope:
web/src/engine/interview.js plus a starter question bank. This is what turns the app from a form into an interview.

web/kb/questions.json -- a DATA question bank (hand-authored, ~12 questions is enough for P1; the full ~30 is the user's K-4 content task). Each question: { id, prompt, why, field (a path into the Experiment), type ('text'|'choice'|'number'|'multi'), options?, askWhen? (a C1-2 predicate), priority (number, lower = asked earlier), tag (the provenance tag an answer gets, default 'user') }. Include the questions that unlock the demo: experiment type, sample/specimen, magnification, markers, replicates, factors, date. `why` is mandatory on every question -- the parent plan's principle is explaining the reasoning, and a question a researcher cannot see the point of is a question they abandon.

web/src/engine/interview.js exports:
  loadQuestions(raw) -> {questions, issues}  -- validate ids are unique and non-empty, `field` is a non-empty string, type is known, choice/multi have non-empty options; report issues rather than throwing.
  nextQuestions(questions, experiment, limit) -> [question]  -- the askable ones, in priority order: askWhen passes (via C1-2 evaluatePredicate), the target slot is not already filled by a STRONG source, and the question has not been skipped. Never return more than `limit`.
  recordAnswer(experiment, question, value) -> {path, value, tag}  -- returns the write DESCRIPTOR rather than performing it, so the store (and its provenance gate) stays the single writer. This keeps the engine pure and testable.
  skipQuestion(experiment, questionId) / isSkipped(...)  -- every question must be skippable (a bench tool that forces 40 answers is opened once and never again), recorded in experiment.provenance.skipped.
  interviewProgress(questions, experiment) -> {answered, askable, skipped, total}.

A question whose slot is already filled by a STRONG tag ('user'/'user_edited'/'imported') is NOT re-asked. A slot filled only by 'freetext' (WEAK, from C1-4) IS still asked -- but the question must carry the parsed value forward as a suggested default so the user is confirming rather than retyping. That confirm-don't-retype path is the whole reason the free-text tier and the interview compose.

INVARIANTS: imports only from engine/predicate.js and core/paths.js; NO store import and no writes -- recordAnswer returns a descriptor; no DOM; no top-level await; unique top-level symbol names across web/src/**.
tasks.verification: `node --test web/tests/*.test.js` passes. Prove by executed assertion: a question whose askWhen predicate is false is NOT returned; a question whose target slot holds a 'user' tag is NOT re-asked; a question whose slot holds only a 'freetext' tag IS still returned AND carries the parsed value as its suggested default; skipping a question removes it from nextQuestions and lands in experiment.provenance.skipped; nextQuestions respects both priority order and `limit`; recordAnswer writes NOTHING (assert the experiment object is deeply unchanged after calling it) and returns a descriptor whose tag is the question's tag. Prove loadQuestions reports (not throws) on duplicate ids and on a choice question with no options. Prove the committed web/kb/questions.json actually loads with ZERO issues -- an invalid shipped question bank must fail the suite. Finally prove the fatigue guard: with an empty Experiment, nextQuestions(..., limit=8) returns at most 8 and includes the questions needed to render a filename.

tasks.title: P1 vertical slice: paste a paragraph, answer questions, get sample IDs and filenames
tasks.scope:
Wire P1 into the running app and PROVE the demoable outcome end to end. Per repo lesson 4 the UI-wiring task is historically the riskiest in any batch, so it is deliberately last and alone in its own batch.

web/src/ui/steps/describe.js -- the paste-a-paragraph step. A large textarea bound to experiment.narrative.text; a 'Read it' action running C1-4 parseFreeText against C1-1's index; the resulting proposals rendered as a REVIEWABLE list (value, the evidence substring that produced it, and Accept / Dismiss per row) -- never silently auto-applied. This project has already shipped a silent-auto-apply defect once (the T10 describer-override work); proposals are suggestions until a human accepts them. Accepting writes through the store with the proposal's 'freetext' tag; the user editing the value afterwards writes 'user_edited'.

web/src/ui/steps/design.js -- factors/levels/replicates entry plus the live condition table from C1-5: each row's sample ID and the filename that row would produce (compose C1-5 buildSampleId into the existing engine/naming.js renderName). Design issues from conditionIssues render inline through the same issue list style the naming step already uses.

Interview surface: render C1-3 nextQuestions (limit 8) wherever it fits the flow best -- a compact panel on the describe step is fine for P1 -- with each question showing its `why`, a Skip control, and a suggested default when one came from free text. Answers go through store.setPath with the question's tag so C0-2's provenance gate governs them.

web/src/main.js -- register the new steps in the router alongside the existing naming step, in flow order (describe -> design -> naming). Load the KB once at startup from globalThis.__MICRONAUT_KB__ (the ONLY place that global is read) via C1-1 loadKb/indexKb, and surface KB issues through the shell's existing toast rather than the console. Keep init() synchronous -- top-level await is forbidden and the build gate will hard-fail on it.

web/styles/app.css -- styles for the textarea, the proposal review rows and the condition table. Extend the existing custom-property palette; do not introduce new hardcoded colours, and keep the @media print block working (the condition table is exactly the kind of thing that belongs on a printed bench card).

INVARIANTS: vanilla DOM only -- NO innerHTML with dynamic or user data anywhere (the pasted paragraph is untrusted text and goes straight into the DOM); no fetch(); no top-level await; unique top-level symbol names across web/src/**; every feature works with the LLM off (there is no LLM in P1 at all).
